summary.text: A Paris appeals court has ordered French actor Gérard Depardieu to stand trial for the alleged rape of actress Charlotte Arnould in 2018. He has denied any wrongdoing. The ruling comes shortly after he abandoned his appeal of an earlier sexual assault conviction.

stories.title: Baghdad moves to take control of Kurdish oil and border crossings, sparking protests

articles.headline: Iraq’s Prime Minister Aims to Wrest More Power From Kurdistan Region
articles.snippet: Ali al-Zaidi, who just scored a symbolic victory against a powerful Iran-backed militia, has now moved to assert control over Kurdish border crossings and oil resources.

articles.headline: Iraq denies sending troops to Kurdistan as crisis talks begin
articles.snippet: Iraq's central government moved to calm fears of a confrontation with the semi-autonomous Kurdistan region on Thursday, denying reports that army units were advancing north. Authorities said an…

articles.headline: How Baghdad's takeover of Kurdistan oil can be detrimental for Iraq and the region
articles.snippet: On Tuesday, Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi ordered moving army units towards the Kurdistan region of Iraq, to assert federal control over its border crossings as well as oilfields under Kurdish…

articles.headline: How an oil feud is deepening rift between Baghdad and Iraq’s Kurdish region
articles.snippet: Prime Minister al-Zaidi's move to take control of border crossings and oilfields has drawn a sharp response from Erbil.

articles.headline: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings
articles.snippet: Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region, waving flags and voicing opposition to plans for the federal government to take control of oil operations and…

agreed_facts.text: The federal government in Baghdad has moved to take control of the Kurdistan region's border crossings and oil operations or oilfields.
The move is attributed to Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.
The move has met opposition in the Kurdish region, through a sharp response from Erbil and street protests.

headline_quotes.quote: Wrest More Power From Kurdistan Region
just scored a symbolic victory against a powerful Iran-backed militia

emphasis.text: Presents the move as the prime minister seeking more power, following a symbolic victory over an Iran-backed militia.

headline_quotes.quote: Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan
Thousands have gathered in the capital of northern Iraq's semiautonomous Kurdish region

emphasis.text: Leads with protests by thousands in the Kurdish regional capital, waving flags and opposing the federal plans.

omissions.text: Does not mention the protests by thousands in the Kurdish regional capital.
Does not mention the prime minister's recent symbolic victory against an Iran-backed militia.

headline_quotes.quote: Iraq’s Prime Minister Aims to Wrest More Power From Kurdistan Region
Protests in Iraqi Kurdistan at plans for government in Baghdad to take over oil, border crossings

emphasis.text: Focuses on the prime minister's bid for power and the protest response in the Kurdish region.

headline_quotes.quote: Iraq denies sending troops to Kurdistan as crisis talks begin
deepening rift between Baghdad and Iraq’s Kurdish region
can be detrimental for Iraq and the region

emphasis.text: Foregrounds fears of a confrontation, the question of army units moving north and the start of crisis talks.
Describes the dispute as an oil feud deepening a rift between Baghdad and Erbil, with possible harm to Iraq and the region.

summary.text: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi moved to assert federal control over the Kurdistan region's border crossings and oil, drawing a sharp response from Erbil and protests by thousands in the region's capital. Baghdad denied reports that army units were advancing north as crisis talks began.

conclusion.text: All sides report Baghdad's move to take control of Kurdish oil and border crossings. The New York Times links it to a win over an Iran-backed militia, DW leads with protests, and East outlets stress the rift and confrontation fears. One The National piece says army units were ordered towards the region; another reports Baghdad denying troops were advancing.

stories.title: Plane crash off Mississippi coast kills six family members

articles.headline: Plane Crashes Off Mississippi Coast, Killing All 6 Passengers
articles.snippet: Six people, including two children, were killed Tuesday after their plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi. The Coast Guard says the bodies of all six people have been recovered, and the cause…

articles.headline: Plane crash off coast of Mississippi kills extended family of six on fishing trip
articles.snippet: Shortly before losing contact with the plane, an air traffic controller at Gulfport–Biloxi International Airport advised the pilot of precipitation and adverse weather in the area

articles.headline: Air traffic controller gave pilot dad chilling warning before plane crash killed 6 family members
articles.snippet: Six family members, including pilot Brent Stokes, died after their Cessna crashed off the Mississippi coast following warnings of bad weather.

articles.headline: Air traffic controller gave pilot dad chilling warning before plane crash killed six family members, including three children aged 10, 12 and 16, on way back from fishing trip
articles.snippet: Brent Stokes, 50, was warned that he faced heavy rains and adverse weather on a flight he took with his family before they crashed near Horn Island, Mississippi on Tuesday afternoon.

agreed_facts.text: Six people were killed when a plane crashed off the coast of Mississippi.
The six people killed were members of one family.
Before the crash, the pilot was warned by an air traffic controller of bad or adverse weather in the area.
The family was on a fishing trip.
Children were among those killed.
The crash happened on Tuesday.

headline_quotes.quote: Killing All 6 Passengers
The Coast Guard says the bodies of all six people have been recovered

emphasis.text: Leads with the death toll, including two children, and the Coast Guard's recovery of all six bodies.

headline_quotes.quote: Air traffic controller gave pilot dad chilling warning
including three children aged 10, 12 and 16
following warnings of bad weather

emphasis.text: Leads with the air traffic controller's weather warning to the pilot, described as a 'chilling warning'.
Names the pilot as Brent Stokes, a father, and gives details such as the Cessna aircraft and the Horn Island location.

omissions.text: Left coverage does not mention the air traffic controller's weather warning to the pilot.
Left coverage does not mention that the victims were members of one family or name the pilot.
Right coverage does not mention the Coast Guard's statement that all six bodies were recovered.

contested_claims.claim: The number of children among the six killed is given as two by one outlet and three by another.

headline_quotes.quote: Plane Crashes Off Mississippi Coast, Killing All 6 Passengers
Air traffic controller gave pilot dad chilling warning

emphasis.text: Emphasises the death toll and, in two articles, the controller's warning to the pilot, named as Brent Stokes.

headline_quotes.quote: kills extended family of six on fishing trip
advised the pilot of precipitation and adverse weather in the area

emphasis.text: Describes the victims as an extended family on a fishing trip and notes the warning came from a controller at Gulfport–Biloxi International Airport.

summary.text: Six people, described as members of one family, were killed on Tuesday when their plane crashed off the Mississippi coast. An air traffic controller had warned the pilot, Brent Stokes, of adverse weather beforehand. The Coast Guard says all six bodies have been recovered.

conclusion.text: All outlets report six people killed in a plane crash off the Mississippi coast. Right-leaning and the East outlet lead with the controller's weather warning, while the left outlet leads with the toll and Coast Guard recovery. The number of children killed is given as two in one report and three in another.

stories.title: Israeli judges suggest dropping key charges in Netanyahu corruption trial

articles.headline: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
articles.snippet: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is accused of bribery, fraud and breach of trust in a long-running trial that has divided the country. He denies all wrongdoing.

articles.headline: Netanyahu declares corruption trial has 'fallen apart' after judges question key charges
articles.snippet: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared his corruption trial "fell apart" as judges urged prosecutors to rethink the bribery and fraud cases.

articles.headline: In Blow To Prosecutors, Israeli Judges Recommend Dropping Key Charges Against Netanyahu
articles.snippet: Netanyahu called the court’s recommendation a “ray of light for truth and justice.”

articles.headline: Daily Briefing Nov. 26: Netanyahu trial collapsing as judges pillory key charges
articles.snippet: Diplomatic correspondent Lazar Berman on the court's bombshell statements about the cases against the premier, and the race to form a government without him

agreed_facts.text: Israeli judges suggested dropping, or questioned, key charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in his corruption trial.
The charges include bribery and fraud.
Netanyahu welcomed the judges' move.

headline_quotes.quote: Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu
a long-running trial that has divided the country
In Blow To Prosecutors

emphasis.text: Leads with the judges' recommendation and describes it as a blow to prosecutors.
Sets out the charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust, notes the trial has divided the country and that Netanyahu denies wrongdoing.
Quotes Netanyahu calling the recommendation a "ray of light for truth and justice".

headline_quotes.quote: Netanyahu declares corruption trial has 'fallen apart'
judges urged prosecutors to rethink the bribery and fraud cases

emphasis.text: Leads with Netanyahu's declaration that his trial has fallen apart.
Describes the judges as urging prosecutors to rethink the bribery and fraud cases.

omissions.text: Does not mention that Netanyahu denies all wrongdoing or that the trial has divided the country.

headline_quotes.quote: Netanyahu declares corruption trial has 'fallen apart'
In Blow To Prosecutors
Judges in Israel Suggest Dropping Key Corruption Case Against Netanyahu

emphasis.text: Focuses on the judges' recommendation, the charges and Netanyahu's reaction.

headline_quotes.quote: Netanyahu trial collapsing as judges pillory key charges
the race to form a government without him

emphasis.text: Describes the trial as collapsing and the court's statements as bombshell.
Links the development to a race to form a government without Netanyahu.

summary.text: Judges in Netanyahu's corruption trial suggested dropping key charges, including bribery and fraud cases, or urged prosecutors to rethink them. Netanyahu, who denies all wrongdoing, said the trial had fallen apart and called the recommendation a ray of light.

conclusion.text: All outlets report judges suggesting dropping or questioning key charges against Netanyahu. Left-leaning outlets frame it as a blow to prosecutors and note his denial, the right-leaning outlet leads with his claim the trial fell apart, and the East-bloc outlet adds the race to form a government without him. No claims are contested.
